- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 70), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overcorrects after mean reversion; if true outcome shows slow recovery, forecast should be slightly conservative (−0.5 to −1.5%).
- For 30-day horizon, if last 3–5 days show strong sentiment + price momentum, model often fails to capture lagged effect; delay peak forecast by 1–2 days if sentiment remains positive.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model tends to average out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
